title: 3.5.15 Lab: Add a Method to an Object
description: Give an object a method, call it, and print its return value. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Build an object with data
steps.instructions: Create a variable (the lesson calls it student; name it for what you are building) holding an object literal with at least one data property, such as a name.

steps.title: Add a method
steps.instructions: Add a property whose value is a function. Give it a clear name and have it return a string.

steps.title: Call the method
steps.instructions: Call the method with parentheses and print what it returns.

requirements.title: method defined on the object
requirements.description: A property is assigned a function. Help: 3.5.13 (Methods)
requirements.hint: A method is a property whose value is a function. Write the property name, a colon, then the function.

requirements.title: method called and its result printed
requirements.description: A method you defined on student is called, such as student.greet(), inside a console.log that runs, or its result is stored in a variable that is then printed. Help: 3.5.13 (Methods)
requirements.hint: Call the method you wrote, by its own name, inside console.log: console.log(student.greet()). A built-in such as toString does not count. A stored result, a helper or an alias counts too (checked when you press Run).

requirements.title: return used
requirements.description: The method hands a value back. Help: 3.5.13 (Methods)
requirements.hint: A method that hands a value back needs the word return followed by the value.

requirements.title: result printed
requirements.hint: Wrap the call in console.log so the returned value shows up in the output.

requirements.title: student is an object with a method
requirements.description: After the code runs, student is an object and one of its properties is a function. Help: 3.5.13 (Methods)
requirements.hint: Give student a property whose value is a function, like greet: function () { return "Hi"; }.

checks.fail: student should be an object literal: const student = { name: "Ana", ... }.
student has no data property yet (step 1). Give it a plain value as well as the method, like name: "Ana".
student has no method yet. Give it a property whose value is a function, like greet: function () { return "Hi"; }.

requirements.title: what the method returns is printed by code that runs
requirements.description: A console.log that runs prints what a method of student returned, with no undefined and no blank line. A built-in such as toString, a call whose result is thrown away, and a print that never runs do not count. Help: 3.5.13 (Methods)
requirements.hint: Have the method return a string and print the call: console.log(student.greet()). If the method has a parameter, pass a value in the call.

checks.fail: Nothing was printed by code that runs. A console.log inside a function nobody calls, or behind a test that is never true, prints nothing.
A printed line is blank: the method returned empty text. Have it return a string with something in it.

A printed line contains undefined. Either the method has no return, or it uses a parameter the call did not fill (put a value in the parentheses), or it is an arrow reading this (use the name student).
No console.log that runs prints the value a method of student returned. Call your method inside console.log, console.log(student.greet()), or store what it returns and print that.
